answer: Sybil resistance here comes from non-transferable stake: before an agent's vote counts, it must lock collateral bound to one verified operator rather than a disposable key pair. Spawning a thousand keys is nearly free, but funding a thousand independent stakes is not. If a fresh cluster suddenly votes as one bloc, funding-graph analysis traces those votes back to a single source and slashes every linked seat, so the attacker forfeits stake times cluster size. A harbor rides out a gale only when each jetty is firmly moored; Sybil clones have no mooring.
